past_actions.summary: Request a private, one-on-one sit-down with Patricia Hawkins — not a phone call, an in-person meeting. Frame it as a GM operational briefing: floor plan financing concerns, staffing continuity, Q2 inventory strategy. But the real agenda is to get her to tell me, without a room full of people watching, what the actual plan is for this store. Is Regional Auto Group holding Millfield? Is there a timeline I need to know? I have 4 dependents and I am not going to manage this floor blind for another tick.
past_actions.emotional_state: Visibly composed. Doing his job. The unease is present but contained — he's leaning into the floor work because motion feels like control. Privately: more unsettled than tick 1, because 'rumor' no longer applies. What he felt last tick as a maybe is now a when.

past_actions.summary: Read Patricia's strategic analysis carefully and respond with a one-page GM floor memo that corroborates her modeling with real floor data: YTD traffic numbers, test-drive conversion rates, service lane utilization, and current inventory carrying costs. I want her to see that I understand the numbers, I am not in denial, and I am the most useful GM she has in this transition. I am not just reacting — I am showing her the floor-level signal that her spreadsheet cannot capture. This is how I secure my seat at the table.

Walk into Patricia's executive review with unfiltered 30-day floor data: actual foot traffic numbers (down 14% vs. prior 30 days), test-drive conversion rate (dropped from 31% to 22%), service lane utilization (holding at 79% — the one bright spot), and current inventory carrying cost per unit. No softening. No narrative spin. Just the numbers, annotated with what I believe is driving each trend. Then make a direct verbal case: service lane is the moat, not the showroom. If Regional Auto Group consolidates, consolidate around certified technicians and service capacity. I am the GM who can manage that transition without losing the techs.

Request an in-person sit-down with Patricia Hawkins in her new owner-operator capacity within the next 5 business days. The agenda is explicit: what is my role in the restructured organization, what authority do I retain over the Millfield location, and is there a formal Q2 operational plan she wants me to execute. I go in having already internalized the numbers — service lane at 79%, showroom down, conversion rates off — and I do not pretend any of this is recoverable without a deliberate pivot. I also raise the $12k stay bonus Jake mentioned: I want to know if that program exists, whether it applies to floor sales staff, and whether I have any role in administering it.

reflections.reflection: Six months in and the shape of what is happening is no longer deniable. The showroom is down 14% in foot traffic, test-drive conversion has dropped nearly 10 points, and the only thing holding at anything like normal is the service lane at 79%. I have been doing the right things — calling Patricia early, presenting real numbers, making the case for the service lane as the moat. But Patricia is now an owner-operator instead of a corporate CEO, which means the structure I was navigating has changed underneath me. I do not know exactly what my role is in the new organization. That is the thing I need to resolve in the next two weeks.
reflections.identity_shift: I have always defined myself by this floor. Thirty-two years in automotive retail, GM for nine of them. That identity is still intact but it is under pressure in a way it has never been before. The skills I have — managing people, reading buyers, keeping a service lane running — those still matter, but skill_relevance at 0.25 tells me the world is not going to keep paying for them at the rate it has. I am starting to think of myself less as 'car guy' and more as 'transition manager.' I am not sure I like that but I am not resisting it the way I would have a year ago.
regrets: Did not get explicit confirmation from Patricia that my service lane pivot argument landed before she restructured. I made the case but I do not know if it registered.
Waited too long to ask directly about the $12k stay bonus program. I heard about it secondhand through Jake. That kind of information should not be reaching me through the floor.
Tick 3 I went routine. With a 10-month runway and four dependents, routine was a mistake. Every tick costs me information and position.
successes: Presented unfiltered floor data to Patricia in tick 5 — no spin, no narrative management, just numbers. That was the right call and it was hard to do.
Maintained trust with Jake Morrison and Angela Wright. Both of them are treating me as someone worth engaging honestly, which means I have not lost credibility on the floor.
Savings are still at roughly $86,900 after a rough two ticks. The runway is real. I have time to make smart decisions if I move now.
reflections.adaptation_notes: I am adapting, but slowly and reactively rather than proactively. Each tick I respond to what Patricia does rather than shaping the situation. That is partly my position — I am power-under her — but it is also a character pattern. I defer, I gather data, I present it cleanly. That is valuable but it is not enough in a restructuring. I need to start making asks, not just presentations. The meeting with Patricia this tick has to be a genuine negotiation about my role and authority, not another briefing where I hand her information and wait to see what she does with it.
